text:
Anna M: Hey team — escalating a customer report: their service saw a burst of 5xxs and repeated SDK retries starting ~11:23 UTC. Customer timeline attached in ticket #5821.
Devon K: what error codes are they seeing exactly? 502/504 or upstream timeouts?
Anna M: 502 and intermittent 504s. Customer observed long tails of failed requests and the SDK retry loop sent ~4x requests for some user flows, causing billing anxiety. They say it coincided with an ISP maintenance window.
Customer: Jane D: Logs from our side show TCP connections being torn down by our edge NAT every ~20s. When that happens, our client sees the streaming request abort mid-response and then the SDK retries immediately — it triggers duplicate tokens use/cost.
Liam (ops-oncall): tagging in case there's an infra-side symptom: @ops-oncall. Any gateway logs for that window?
Support Bot: Attached: gateway access logs (s3://prod-logs/support/5821/gateway-1798200000.log) and short trace IDs: trace-9c3, trace-9c4, trace-9c7.
Liam (ops-oncall): Pulling traces now. Initial look: TCP FIN from customer IPs followed by 502/gateway reset at our edge LB. We also see ephemeral backend connection pool exhaustion warnings around the same time in the autoscaler metrics.
Devon K: Could be our backend keepalive behavior + customer NAT session timeout (eviction) => client reconnects are landing on existing but closed backend sockets, causing 502s. Do we see `connection_reset_by_peer` in logs?
Liam (ops-oncall): yes, multiple `ECONNRESET` and `stream aborted` entries. Also a small spike in TIME_WAIT on the edge.
Anna M: Customer gave repro steps. They ran a tight loop of the JS SDK with streaming enabled. Steps: 1) create streaming request; 2) intentionally drop underlying TCP (simulate NAT eviction); 3) SDK auto-retries immediately; 4) second connection races and gets 502. They provided a minimal repro snippet.
Customer: Jane D: repro (abridged):
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.KEY });
async function run() {
  try {
    const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'r-instruct-1', input: 'ping' });
    // kill underlying connection via iptables rule after 10s to mimic NAT eviction
  } catch (e) {
    console.log('err', e);
  }
}
run();
```
Devon K: Thanks. I want to reproduce from our side without needing iptables: I'll run a curl with `--http2` and then close the socket from a client proxy so we can see behavior. Also will try forcing `Connection: close` header to see if that reduces pooled socket reuse issues.
Liam (ops-oncall): FYI set of mitigation ideas: 1) make gateway detect client TCP FIN and fail fast to avoid backend stuck sockets; 2) adjust keepalive to shorter on gateway-backend leg; 3) implement a small randomized retry jitter client-side so simultaneous retries don't pile onto an already degraded pool.
Anna M: Customer asked for immediate mitigation while we investigate: can we recommend a client config change they can deploy quickly?
Devon K: Recommend SDK quick patch: set retryBackoff with jitter (200ms-800ms), reduce concurrent streaming connections per socket to 1, and set `Connection: close` for clients behind aggressive NATs. Also set a shorter socket timeout (e.g., 15s) to prevent long-lived broken sockets.
Customer: Jane D: we can push that in a fix tonight if it helps. Also can collect pcap if you need it.
Liam (ops-oncall): Please do capture pcap of 3 failed sessions (pcap + timestamp) and share via secure upload. I'll correlate with gateway traces.
Devon K: Reproduced locally: when I inject a TCP FIN at ~8-10s into an active stream, the gateway returns `HTTP/2 502` on the next client connection that races for the same backend connection. Root cause hypothesis: connection pool entry reused to talk to backend socket in half-closed state.
Anna M: Are there any quick server-side changes we can do? Rolling change to make connection pool validate socket liveness before reusing?
Liam (ops-oncall): We can enable an optional health check flag on the pool to do a one-byte ping before reuse, but that adds ~5-10ms per new logical request. For affected customers we can roll it as a targeted config in the next deploy.
Devon K: Also can add ephemeral per-socket generation IDs so when a backend socket becomes half-closed we don't accidentally reuse it. That's medium-term.
Customer: Jane D: If you can toggle something server-side that avoids reuse temporarily, we'd accept the perf hit over duplicate charges.
Anna M: Ok I'll propose the server-side toggle + the SDK recommendations. Customer ok with a short perf hit.
Support Bot: Update: escalated to infra team; internal ticket INF-2645 created.
Liam (ops-oncall): Patch plan: 1) enable `pool.validate_on_reuse=true` for the customer's tenant via config flag; 2) monitor error rate for 30m; 3) if stable, consider broader rollout. ETA for change: 45min.
Devon K: I'll prepare a Canary build with the `validate_on_reuse` toggle and test with the repro snippet. Also adding a temporary 50ms accept-delay between retries to reduce retry storm.
Anna M: Communications: I'll draft a message for the customer: explain root cause hypothesis (NAT eviction + connection pool reuse), list recommended client change (retry jitter, `Connection: close`, lower timeout), and offer the server-side toggle until we ship a safer pool fix.
Customer: Jane D: thank you. we'll enable the SDK changes and push logs + pcap. Please keep me posted.
Liam (ops-oncall): Change pushed to staging; running canary against their tenant ID. Early telemetry: error rate down 70% for the canary traffic.
Devon K: Good signal. I'll run a 10-minute aggressive repro against the canary to see if we still hit races.
Support Bot: Action log: INF-2645 updated -> keepalive/pool-validate toggle applied to tenant `acct_01G2`.
Devon K: After 10m stress, repro fails to trigger the same 502 pattern — pool validation seems to avoid half-closed reuse.
Anna M: I'll send the customer the mitigation steps + timeline for a permanent runtime patch (we want pool-generation IDs + better half-close detection).
Customer: Jane D: confirmed behavior improved on our side. We'll leave SDK jitter in place as a precaution. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :heart:
Liam (ops-oncall): We'll keep monitoring for 24h and then mark incident as mitigated if no regression.
Anna M: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and move to postmortem prep if things stay green. :thumbsup:
